name: Shopify Admin API (Customer amountSpent + Order/fulfillment status + order webhooks)
provides: Would supply the real values behind Tideover's two hardcoded fields for any Shopify-based merchant: Customer.ltvCents (lib/types.ts:208) from the Customer.amountSpent{amount,currencyCode} field, and Order.orderValueCents/status (lib/types.ts:122,126) from Order totalPriceSet + displayFulfillmentStatus/displayFinancialStatus. Order webhooks (orders/create, orders/updated, orders/fulfilled) would give a live replacement for the CSV-import/onboarding-wizard path for Shopify merchants specifically (crowdfunding merchants with no Shopify store still have no such source and stay on CSV import).
apiModel: Shopify Admin API, GraphQL only for any new integration work — REST Admin API has been legacy since 2024-10-01 and Shopify requires GraphQL for all new/custom apps as of 2025-04-01, so build against GraphQL from day one. Customer object exposes `amountSpent { amount currencyCode }` (per-customer total spend — exactly the LTV Tideover needs) and `numberOfOrders`; query via `customers(first:N){ nodes { amountSpent{amount currencyCode} } }` or a single `customer(id:)` lookup keyed off a webhook's customer id. Order object exposes `totalPriceSet`/`currentTotalPriceSet` (order value), `displayFulfillmentStatus` (fulfilled/partial/unfulfilled) and `displayFinancialStatus` (paid/pending/refunded) — order value + order/fulfillment status. Data arrives live via Admin-API-managed webhook subscriptions (orders/create, orders/updated, orders/fulfilled, orders/paid); there is no dedicated "customer LTV changed" webhook, so a real LTV refresh means re-querying amountSpent on every order webhook for that customer, not a push of the LTV value itself.
authModel: Two real paths. (1) Custom app / single-store static token — merchant (or Dylan, on his own dev store) creates an app scoped to just that store, grants read_customers + read_orders (+ read_fulfillments), and gets a static Admin API access token immediately on install, no OAuth redirect dance. This is the realistic near-term path for Tideover's current forward-only-email pilot model. Caveat found in research: as of Jan 2026 Shopify no longer lets merchants create *new* custom apps from the plain Settings UI — new custom apps must be created via the Partner/Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI — but the result is still a single static token per store once installed, not full multi-tenant OAuth. (2) Public/OAuth app — needed only if Tideover later wants a self-serve "Connect your Shopify" button across many merchants: requires a free Partner account, app registration, redirect URI, and standard OAuth 2.0 code exchange plus HMAC-verified webhook registration. Given Tideover's current product stance (marketing copy explicitly promises "no OAuth, no passwords, no Shopify admin" — components/marketing/FAQ.tsx:47-48), adding either path is a positioning reversal, not just an engineering task.
trialPath: Fully free. Create a free Shopify Partner account, then create a free Development Store from the Partner dashboard (no time limit, unlimited, cannot take real payments but supports the built-in Bogus Gateway to place fake paid test orders). Install a custom app on that dev store to get a real token and real customer/order objects for testing at zero cost.
howToTest: Cheapest end-to-end path: Partner account (free) -> dev store (free) -> custom app with read_customers + read_orders scopes -> hit the GraphQL endpoint directly with the token to confirm amountSpent, e.g. `{ customers(first:10){ nodes { amountSpent{amount currencyCode} numberOfOrders } } }` — no webhook infra needed just to prove LTV data exists. For webhook/order-flow testing: place a real (fake-money) order on the dev store via Bogus Gateway checkout to fire genuine orders/create with a valid HMAC, or use the admin's per-webhook "Send test notification" button, or `shopify webhook trigger --topic orders/create` via CLI (fast, but its payload has no valid HMAC so it can't verify signature-checking code).
notes: Grep across tideover/ found zero real Shopify wiring anywhere: Channel type (lib/types.ts:16) only has mock/gorgias/tidio/intercom/email, no shopify; the only webhook receiver is the generic helpdesk ticket ingest at app/api/ingest/[channel]/[token]/route.ts -> lib/ingest-route (tickets, not orders/customers); no OAuth route exists in app/api or app/onboarding/ConnectPanel.tsx. Customer.ltvCents is populated only from: seeded fixtures (scripts/gen-seed.mjs:291,366), a flat hardcoded 60000 onboarding default (lib/onboarding.ts:112), or copied from a single CSV row's order value at import time (lib/import.ts:69: `ltvCents: row.orderValueCents ?? DEFAULT_ORDER_VALUE_CENTS`) — note this isn't even accumulated across multiple orders for the same customer, so it's not true LTV even for the CSV/Kickstarter path, let alone Shopify. Important product-fit tension: marketing copy (components/marketing/FAQ.tsx:47-48) actively sells the ABSENCE of Shopify access ("no OAuth, no passwords, no Shopify admin... forward-only email") as a trust/low-friction feature. Building real Shopify LTV/order data means adding the exact integration surface the current pilot pitch says Tideover deliberately avoids — this is a Fable-level product call (positioning reversal), not just an engineering ticket. For a pure-Kickstarter/BackerKit merchant with no Shopify store at all, none of this applies — CSV import stays the only real data path, and its LTV gap (single-order value, not accumulated) is a separate, cheaper bug worth fixing regardless of Shopify.

name: Gorgias
provides: Ticket content only (subject, body, tags, customer email, optional order_ref) via an outbound automation into Tideover's canonical ingest shape. Does NOT provide per-customer LTV/total-spend — the Gorgias Customer object (developers.gorgias.com/reference/the-customer-object) has no spend/revenue/order-count field; order data only shows up embedded in the `integrations` object when a Shopify/Recharge integration is separately connected in that merchant's Gorgias account, and even then it's per-order line data shown in the ticket sidebar, not an aggregated LTV number exposed by the API. Tideover's ltvCents (lib/types.ts:208, used by lib/engines/gift.ts:31 for the gift/risk feature) would still need Shopify's Admin API (customer.amountSpent) as a second integration; Gorgias alone can never answer the LTV question, even for a merchant that has it installed.
apiModel: Two separate mechanisms, easy to conflate: (1) REST API v2 (developers.gorgias.com) for polling — GET /api/tickets, GET /api/customers, the Ticket/Customer/TicketMessage objects — auth'd with an API key or OAuth2 bearer. (2) 'HTTP Integrations' (Settings > Account > HTTP integration), Gorgias's outbound-automation feature, which is the closest thing to a webhook: it POSTs a templated body (using variables like {{ticket.customer.email}}, {{ticket.last_message.body_text}}, {{ticket.tags}}) to a URL you control, on triggers Ticket created / Ticket updated / Ticket message created / etc. Auth on that outbound call is either a static custom header (e.g. Authorization: Bearer <key>) or OAuth2 client-credentials — there is NO per-request computed signature. I could not find any Gorgias doc describing a dynamic HMAC-signed webhook body (searched 'X-Gorgias-Signature', signatures, webhooks+signing across developers.gorgias.com and docs.gorgias.com); the only 'Signatures' doc page that exists is about email/agent signatures, unrelated.
authModel: For pulling data (polling mode): a private-app API key, generated at Settings > Account > REST API in the merchant's own Gorgias account (username + API key password) -- Dylan doesn't need Gorgias's approval, the merchant self-serves this. For push (HTTP Integration outbound), Gorgias is the one calling Tideover, so 'auth' from Tideover's side means checking a static shared header value the merchant pastes into the HTTP Integration's Header field -- not a cryptographic signature. A full listed OAuth2 public app (Gorgias App Store) needs a registered Developer Portal app with Client ID/Secret and Gorgias approval -- unnecessary for single-merchant bolt-on use; only relevant if Tideover wants to be an installable Gorgias marketplace app later.
trialPath: 7-day free trial at gorgias.com/signup, full features, no credit card required -- enough to create a live helpdesk, generate a real ticket, and fire a real HTTP Integration. A persistent developer/Sandbox account is a heavier, manual path: register at partners.gorgias.com/signup (Developer Portal), then you must already have a 'draft app' submitted before Gorgias support will convert your trial into a Sandbox/Developer account (support contact, per developers.gorgias.com/docs/1-register-on-developer-portal) -- only worth doing if building a listed public app, not for verifying the ingest path.
howToTest: Cheapest real end-to-end test: start the 7-day trial, go to Settings > Account > HTTP integration > Add HTTP integration, trigger = 'Ticket created', method POST, Content-Type JSON, body templated to Tideover's canonical shape (external_id: {{ticket.id}}, customer_email: {{ticket.customer.email}}, subject: {{ticket.subject}}, body: {{ticket.last_message.body_text}}, tags: {{ticket.tags}}), point the URL first at webhook.site to see the real rendered payload, then at Tideover's POST /api/ingest/[channel]/[token] running with DEMO_MODE not set to 'false' (accepts unsigned traffic per lib/ingest-route.ts:71-73) so you don't hit the HMAC gap below. Create one real ticket (email the trial helpdesk's support address) to fire the trigger and confirm it lands as a ticket in Tideover.
notes: Code check: lib/channel-adapters/GorgiasAdapter.ts is a documented STUB -- listTickets and authCallback both throw NotImplementedError (lines 29-31, 73-75); only normalizeInbound (line 38) and verifyWebhook (line 56, checks X-Gorgias-Signature HMAC) are implemented. But verifyWebhook is dead weight for a real launch: it's wired only into the LEGACY app/api/ticket-ingest/route.ts:80 (getAdapter(channel).verifyWebhook(...)), and that whole route returns 410 gone once DEMO_MODE=false (route.ts:55-60). The actual production ingest path, app/api/ingest/[channel]/[token]/route.ts -> lib/ingest-route.ts, never calls any ChannelAdapter at all -- it only checks Tideover's OWN HMAC (lib/webhook-secret.ts, X-Tideover-Signature derived from the merchant's inboxToken). That's a real gap for Gorgias specifically: per current docs, Gorgias's HTTP Integrations can only attach a STATIC header or OAuth2 bearer to an outbound call -- it cannot compute a per-request HMAC over its own templated body, so a live Gorgias merchant can never satisfy lib/ingest-route.ts's 'live mode requires verifyWebhookSig or 401' gate (ingest-route.ts:73-81) as built. Closing this needs one of: (a) Fable decides to add a static-shared-secret auth path alongside HMAC for helpdesk-templated channels (touches the ingest security gate, a high-risk file per CLAUDE.md), or (b) a thin relay (e.g. a small Cloudflare Worker) that receives Gorgias's plain POST and re-signs it before forwarding to Tideover. Separately and more importantly: even a fully-wired Gorgias integration only ever supplies ticket text, never LTV -- so the gift/risk engine's ltvCents stays 100% seed-only (scripts/gen-seed.mjs) or CSV-approximated (lib/import.ts:69, which takes a single row's orderValueCents, not true lifetime spend) for every real merchant, Shopify-backed or Kickstarter-only, until a separate Shopify Admin API integration is built.

apiModel: Real, current REST API (developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing). Key objects: Tickets (`GET/POST /api/v2/tickets`, fields incl. requester_id, tags, custom_fields), Users (`GET /api/v2/users/{id}`) with a `user_fields` bag for admin-defined custom fields, and Webhooks (`POST /api/v2/webhooks`, subscriptions: `conditional_ticket_events` fired by Triggers/Automations, `request_format: "json"`, optional bearer/basic/api-key auth block). Push-based: Zendesk Trigger → Webhook is the standard "ticket tagged → notify URL" path Tideover already targets (no polling needed for ticket events). Monitoring: `GET /api/v2/webhooks/{id}/invocations` and `.../attempts` for delivery/signing debug. Zendesk has NO native per-customer LTV or total-spend field on the Ticket or User object — it is a pure helpdesk, not a commerce system. `user_fields` can hold a merchant-defined "lifetime_value" number, but nothing populates it automatically; it must be written there by an external sync (e.g. a Shopify→Zendesk app, or Tideover computing LTV itself from Shopify order data and pushing it back as a Zendesk user field). Zendesk Sell (separate CRM product, different API/auth) has deal values, but that's pipeline revenue, not customer purchase history — not usable for this.
authModel: Two supported schemes: (1) API token — admin generates one in Admin Center → Apps and integrations → APIs → Zendesk API, used as Basic Auth `{email}/token:{api_token}`; simplest for a single-merchant server-to-server integration, which is what Tideover needs. (2) OAuth 2.0 — register an OAuth client in Admin Center, then either Authorization Code flow (per-user consent, for a multi-tenant public app) or Client Credentials flow (server-to-server, no user present). For Tideover's model (one Tideover-owned webhook receiver per merchant, merchant configures it themselves in their own Zendesk instance), Dylan does NOT need OAuth or a Zendesk-owned app at all — the merchant creates the Trigger + Webhook themselves in their Admin Center pointing at Tideover's `/api/ingest/zendesk/{token}` URL, optionally with the webhook's built-in bearer/basic auth header or Tideover's own HMAC signing (X-Tideover-Signature). No Zendesk credentials touch Tideover's servers at all under this design — auth only matters if Tideover later needs to pull data (e.g. user_fields for LTV) rather than just receive pushed tickets, in which case an API token scoped to a read-only agent is the minimal path.
howToTest: Sign up for Zendesk's 14-day free trial (zendesk.com/register, no credit card, defaults to Suite Professional features) — this alone is a full working Zendesk instance, no separate sandbox needed. In it: (1) create a test ticket, tag it `presale`; (2) Admin Center → Apps and integrations → Webhooks → create a webhook with endpoint = a temporary public URL (e.g. an ngrok tunnel to a locally-run `npm run dev` instance of Tideover, or a request-bin) and `request_format: json`; (3) use the webhook list's built-in "Test webhook" action (Options menu → Test webhook → pick event → Send test) to fire a synthetic payload without needing a real trigger to fire — cheapest possible round trip, no coding required to see the JSON shape Tideover's `zendeskTrigger()` template expects; (4) separately create an actual Trigger (Admin Center → Objects and rules → Triggers) with condition "Tags contains presale" and action "Notify active webhook" to confirm the real tag→push path end-to-end. A true "Sandbox" environment (staging copy of production) is Enterprise-plan-only and not needed for this — the trial account IS the sandbox.
name: Zendesk
notes: Tideover already has real, if unwired, plumbing for this: `tideover/lib/ingest-templates.ts:74-97` (`zendeskTrigger()`) generates the exact copy-paste Trigger+Webhook setup instructions and body template a merchant needs (mapping `{{ticket.id}}`, `{{ticket.requester.email}}`, `{{ticket.title}}`, `{{ticket.description}}`, `{{ticket.tags}}` into Tideover's canonical schema), and `tideover/app/api/onboarding/route.ts:45` + `ConnectPanel.tsx` surface it in the onboarding wizard UI. `tideover/lib/ingest-route.ts:42` allowlists `"zendesk"` as an ingest channel, but per its own comment (line 41) "every canonical webhook flows the `email`-shaped pipeline" — "zendesk" is a cosmetic routing label only, there is no Zendesk-specific parsing, field-mapping validation, or live-ticket pull; it's the same generic signed-JSON ingest endpoint as everything else, driven entirely by what the merchant configures on their end from the instructions text. So: genuinely stubbed, not fake — the integration is architecturally real (push model matches how Zendesk actually works) but has never been tested against a live Zendesk trigger firing real payloads, and the `order_ref` placeholder (`{{ticket.ticket_field_option_title_<order_id>}}`, line 86) is a guess at a custom-field syntax merchants would need to adapt per their own ticket form, not a validated Zendesk placeholder. The bigger gap: even a perfectly wired Zendesk ingest only ever gives Tideover ticket/customer identity (email, order ref, tags) — never LTV, since Zendesk doesn't track purchases. For a Kickstarter/BackerKit merchant with no Shopify, there is no API path to real LTV via Zendesk or any helpdesk; it would have to come from BackerKit's own order data (separate integration) or be manually entered/omitted.
provides: Real-time ticket ingest (subject, body, requester email, tags, ticket ID, created_at) via Trigger→Webhook when a ticket is tagged e.g. `presale` — feeds Tideover's ticket/order_ref/customer_email fields. Does NOT provide LTV, order value, order status, or fulfillment state — Zendesk has no commerce data model. Order status/fulfillment must still come from Shopify (or BackerKit/Kickstarter for crowdfunding merchants); Zendesk is purely the "where is my order" conversation surface, not the source of truth for any order/spend metric Tideover scores risk on.
trialPath: zendesk.com/register — free 14-day trial, no credit card required, provisions a full Suite Professional-featured instance (Admin Center, Triggers, Webhooks, Agent Workspace all included) that can be used as a complete standalone test environment; a dedicated Enterprise-tier "Sandbox" (staging copy of prod) is not needed and isn't available below Enterprise anyway.

apiModel: REST OpenAPI (base api.tidio.com) covering Contacts (GET/POST /contacts, GET/PATCH /contacts/{contactId}, /contacts/{contactId}/properties), Conversations, Operators, and a Tickets/helpdesk surface, plus a separate Webhooks system (event push to a merchant-configured endpoint, e.g. new conversation/new message) documented at developers.tidio.com/reference. No polling-vs-webhook choice for Tideover's ingest model — webhooks are the only near-real-time path since OpenAPI is REST/pull. Contact object exposes only default identity fields (email, first_name, last_name, phone, distinct_id) plus an open custom "properties" bag operators/bots can set — there is NO built-in purchase/order/revenue/lifetime-value field. Any LTV would have to be a custom property the merchant (or Tideover) pushes in from Shopify/BackerKit themselves; Tidio does not source or expose per-customer spend natively. Rate limits are not published in the surfaced docs.
authModel: OpenAPI auth is a Client-Id/Client-Secret header pair (X-Tidio-Openapi-Client-Id, X-Tidio-Openapi-Client-Secret) issued per-workspace under Settings → Developer → OpenAPI in the Tidio panel — not classic OAuth, not a single "project token" as Tideover's code comment claims. Webhooks are configured separately under Settings → Developer → Webhooks with a Tidio-issued signing/secret mechanism. Critically, both OpenAPI and Webhooks are gated to the Plus/Premium subscription tier — the Settings → Developer → OpenAPI/Webhooks panel is reportedly not even visible on Free/Starter/Growth plans, so Dylan cannot self-serve a credential pair without upgrading to Plus first.
howToTest: Cheapest real path: sign up for Tidio's Free plan (50 conversations/mo) and install the chat widget on a throwaway/dev site to confirm the conversation/contact JSON shape by generating a real chat manually — this validates `normalizeInbound` field-mapping assumptions for free. But this does NOT validate the actual ingest pipeline: Settings → Developer → OpenAPI/Webhooks is reportedly locked out below Plus (~$749/mo, sales-gated per pricing pages found), so there is no self-serve way to fire a real webhook into `/api/ingest` or call the Contacts API without either paying for Plus or emailing Tidio sales/support to request a time-boxed trial credential for evaluation. No dev-store or sandbox tier exists for the API layer itself.
name: Tidio
notes: Biggest finding: Tidio's entire API surface (OpenAPI + Webhooks) is paywalled behind the Plus plan, which pricing pages put at roughly $749/mo with a 12x jump from the $59/mo Growth tier and no self-serve middle tier — this is already ~equal to or above Dylan's entire $750 total budget and is wildly disproportionate to what a small crowdfunding/presale merchant (Tideover's actual ICP) would spend on a helpdesk. Practically, that makes Tidio a poor real integration target: even if Tideover builds the adapter fully, the merchant would need a $749+/mo Tidio subscription just to unlock the webhook/API needed to feed tickets in. Separately, and independent of pricing, Tidio's Contact object has no native LTV/order-value/revenue field — confirming Dylan's central LTV question resolves the same way here as elsewhere: LTV must come from Shopify/BackerKit/CSV and be joined by email, never from the helpdesk itself. In the code: lib/channel-adapters/TidioAdapter.ts:21-52 — listTickets and sendReply both throw NotImplementedError (ChannelAdapter.ts:54-61); normalizeInbound (line 30-46) is a real field-mapper stub (conversation_id→externalId, visitor.email→customerEmail, message.content→body) but untested against live payloads; verifyWebhook (line 48-52) just string-compares a header `x-tidio-secret` to `process.env.TIDIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — this is a placeholder guess, not Tidio's actual signature/HMAC verification scheme, and hasn't been confirmed against real Tidio webhook headers. The file's own doc-comment ("Tidio uses project API tokens (no OAuth dance)") is inaccurate versus the real Client-Id/Client-Secret header auth found in current docs — worth fixing the comment even before any real build-out. registry.ts:17 wires TidioAdapter into the channel registry, but getSendAdapter (registry.ts:31-35) forces all real sends through MockAdapter unless DEMO_FORCE_MOCK_SEND=false, so no live Tidio traffic can leave the demo today regardless.
provides: Ticket ingestion only (conversation/message → Tideover ticket), via webhook push once wired. Does not and cannot provide per-customer LTV/total-spend, order value, order status, or fulfillment data — Tidio has no commerce/revenue object. At best it could carry a merchant-populated custom "property" if the merchant manually or via another integration writes order value into a contact's custom properties, but that's not something Tidio sources itself.
trialPath: No free/self-serve trial found for the API/webhook layer. The chat widget itself is free forever (Free plan, 50 conversations/mo), but Settings → Developer → OpenAPI and Settings → Developer → Webhooks — the only ways to get credentials or receive events — are reported as available only once subscribed to Plus/Premium. The realistic free option is emailing Tidio sales/support to request a short evaluation trial of Plus-tier API access; nothing in the docs confirms an automatic sandbox.

name: Intercom
provides: Ticket ingest (conversation created/replied webhooks → Tideover ticket queue) and, if wired, outbound reply send. Does NOT natively provide per-customer LTV/total-spend — Intercom is a messaging/helpdesk platform, not commerce. The only path to LTV inside Intercom is if the merchant has separately installed Intercom's own Shopify app, which auto-writes `custom_attributes` onto the Contact object (lifetime spend, total order count, last order date, last order status) whenever a Shopify order fires. Tideover has no code today that reads Contacts/custom_attributes at all — only conversation payloads — so even in that best case it's a net-new fetch to build. For a Kickstarter/BackerKit merchant with no Shopify, Intercom has zero spend data period; LTV there can only come from the CSV backer import path, never Intercom.
apiModel: REST + webhooks on api.intercom.io. Inbound: webhook topics like `conversation.user.created`, `conversation.user.replied`, `conversation.admin.assigned` (developers.intercom.com/docs/references/webhooks/webhook-models), payload wrapped in `{data:{item:{...}}}` matching what IntercomAdapter.normalizeInbound already parses. Outbound: `POST /conversations/{id}/reply` with `{message_type:'comment', type:'admin', body}` (documented in the adapter's own header comment). Read: `GET /conversations`, `GET /contacts/{id}` (for custom_attributes/LTV, not currently called anywhere in the repo). Rate limits: 10,000 req/min per app, 25,000/min per workspace, push endpoint capped at 600/min. 5-second webhook response window, 1 retry after 1 min on failure.
authModel: Two paths: (1) OAuth for a public app — authorize at https://app.intercom.com/oauth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=..., exchange code at POST https://api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token (already documented in IntercomAdapter.ts:13-14 comment, but authCallback() at line 65-67 throws NotImplementedError — not built). (2) Simpler for testing: a Personal/Private Access Token generated directly in Developer Hub → Configure → Authentication, no OAuth dance needed, usable immediately for curl/API testing. Webhooks are verified via `X-Hub-Signature` (sha1 HMAC over raw body using the app's client_secret) — this part IS actually implemented and correct: IntercomAdapter.ts:53-63 computes `sha1=` + HMAC-SHA1(client_secret, rawBody) and does a timingSafeEqual compare against the header, reading `INTERCOM_CLIENT_SECRET` from env.
trialPath: Free — Intercom development workspaces are free, unlimited in count, and require no existing paid account (intercom.com/help articles 9086429). Create an app in the Developer Hub against a new dev workspace, generate an Access Token in Configure → Authentication, and subscribe to conversation webhook topics. Dev workspaces are US-region only and lack outbound email/push, but conversations, webhooks, and the Conversations/Contacts REST API all work.
howToTest: Spin up a free dev workspace + app in the Developer Hub, grab the Access Token, and (a) fire a test conversation from the Messenger or via `POST /conversations`, subscribe the webhook to `conversation.user.created`/`conversation.user.replied` pointed at an ngrok tunnel to Tideover's `/api/ticket-ingest?channel=intercom` (or the per-merchant `/api/ingest/[channel]/[token]` route per ADR-0011), and confirm verifyWebhook's HMAC check passes and normalizeInbound produces a sane NormalizedTicket; (b) separately curl `POST /conversations/{id}/reply` directly with the Access Token to validate the send contract, since IntercomAdapter.sendReply() is currently just a NotImplementedError stub (ChannelAdapter.ts:54-61, IntercomAdapter.ts:28-31) and getSendAdapter() forces all real channels through the MockAdapter for demo sends anyway (registry.ts:31-35).
notes: Current wiring is genuinely half-real, not fully fake: verifyWebhook (IntercomAdapter.ts:53-63) and normalizeInbound (IntercomAdapter.ts:33-51) are correct, working implementations of Intercom's actual webhook contract — they'd pass a real signature check today. But listTickets, sendReply, and authCallback are all bare NotImplementedError throws (IntercomAdapter.ts:24-31,65-67), and the onboarding wizard only lets a merchant pick the "Intercom" label (OnboardingWizard.tsx:21,51; api/onboarding/route.ts:22 zod enum) with zero credential-capture UI behind it — selecting it stores a config value that nothing downstream can act on yet. Effort to reach ingest+send parity with Gorgias/Tidio: three well-documented single-endpoint calls (OAuth token exchange, GET conversations, POST reply) = M. Getting LTV out of Intercom at all is a separate, optional, larger lift: it requires the merchant to already run Intercom's own Shopify app (out of Tideover's control) AND a net-new Contacts-fetch method Tideover doesn't have today — for the crowdfunding side of the ICP (Kickstarter/BackerKit, no Shopify) this path is a dead end entirely; LTV there has to come from the CSV backer import, never from Intercom.

name: BackerKit / Kickstarter backer-list CSV import
provides: email, firstName, customer group (ks-backer/late-pledge/new-preorder), order value in cents (used AS the LTV proxy — `customer.ltvCents`), and an optional merchant-disclosed ETA string. This is the ONLY path that populates Customer/Order data for a Kickstarter or BackerKit merchant (no Shopify order API involved).
apiModel: Neither platform has a real API Tideover can integrate against for this. Kickstarter: no official public API for a creator's own backer/pledge data — the only path is the creator manually clicking 'Backer Report' → 'Download' → 'Export to CSV' in their project dashboard (help.kickstarter.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005135894). Columns: Backer Number, Backer Name, Email, Pledge Amount, Reward Title, Reward Minimum, Shipping fields, Survey Response, Add-ons, SKU, Quantity. That report expires and becomes unreadable (no PII) 2 years after the project's latest estimated-delivery date. There is NO per-customer lifetime-value or total-spend field — 'Pledge Amount' is a single project's pledge, period; a backer who supports the same creator's next campaign shows up as a fresh, unrelated row with no linkage. BackerKit: also no general third-party developer API for pulling backer/pledge records (apitracker.io/a/backerkit shows no auth method, no endpoints, no sandbox listed — all blank). What BackerKit exposes is (a) CSV/Excel exports from its own dashboard 'Exports' tab — an 'Expected Revenue' export (backer ID, name, state, country, pledge level cost, upgrades, add-on cost, shipping cost, tax cost, total cost) and a 'Collected Revenue' export (backer ID, email, state, country, transaction id/date/amount/source) — help.backerkit.com/article/583-overview-of-exports; and (b) narrow one-way API-key integrations to fulfillment partners (ShipStation, Fulfillrite, Shipwire) that push shipping/address data, not financials, and aren't meant for third-party SaaS like Tideover. Bottom line: for both platforms the 'API' Dylan would integrate against is a human clicking export, not a machine-callable endpoint.
authModel: None needed from Dylan/Tideover — there's no OAuth app or API key to register with either platform for this data. The merchant authenticates into their OWN Kickstarter creator dashboard or BackerKit account, downloads the CSV themselves, and uploads that file into Tideover's onboarding wizard. This matches ADR-0010's explicit 'Rung 0' design goal: 'NO OAuth, NO Shopify admin, NO passwords' (docs/adr/ADR-0010-csv-import.md line 7). The raw file is parsed client-side in the browser (tideover/lib/csv.ts) and only the mapped, structured rows are POSTed to /api/import — the merchant's KS/BackerKit credentials never touch Tideover at all.
trialPath: No free sandbox/dev account exists for either platform for this purpose (Kickstarter requires a real funded, completed project to unlock a Backer Report; BackerKit is tied to a paid, launched pledge-manager campaign). The free path is to hand-build two tiny sample CSVs using the EXACT documented column headers: a Kickstarter one (Backer Number, Backer Name, Email, Pledge Amount, Reward Title, Estimated Delivery) and a BackerKit one (Backer ID, Email, Pledge Level, Pledge Total, Estimated Delivery, BackerKit Order ID). These headers already match the alias tables baked into the code (tideover/lib/csv.ts:123-146, KS_ALIASES/BK_ALIASES + KS_SIGNATURE/BK_SIGNATURE at lines 149-162), so a synthetic file is functionally identical to a real export for testing the mapping/import path.
howToTest: Cheapest end-to-end test, no trial account needed: write the two synthetic CSVs described above, run them through the existing parser (tideover/lib/csv.ts: parseCsv → detectFormat → mapRows/mapKickstarterRow/mapBackerkitRow), which is already unit-tested in tideover/lib/__tests__/csv.test.ts and tideover/lib/__tests__/import.test.ts, then walk the onboarding wizard's 'Import your backer list' step (tideover/app/onboarding/ImportPanel.tsx) which previews the mapped rows and POSTs to tideover/app/api/import/route.ts (zod-validated, capped at 2000 rows — IMPORT_ROW_CAP in tideover/lib/import.ts:20), and confirm N customers / N orders get created via importBackerRows (tideover/lib/import.ts:28-133). No repo file currently ships a checked-in sample CSV fixture — worth adding one under tideover/ so this is a repeatable regression test, not a one-off.
notes: IMPORTANT HONESTY GAP tied directly to the gift/LTV question: for CSV-imported customers, `Customer.ltvCents` is NOT a lifetime value — it is set exactly ONCE, at the moment a new customer row is first created, straight from that one row's pledge/order amount, and is NEVER re-summed on a later re-import or a second pledge from the same backer (tideover/lib/import.ts:63-77 only sets ltvCents inside the `if (!customer)` branch; an existing customer created on a prior import keeps its original ltvCents forever, even though a new Order is still created and linked). So a Kickstarter merchant genuinely has no per-customer LTV concept at all beyond 'this one pledge' — which is exactly what the code does, it just labels it 'ltvCents.' Second gap: when a CSV row has no parseable money value, Tideover silently fabricates the 'LTV' as a hardcoded $50 floor (`DEFAULT_ORDER_VALUE_CENTS = 5000`, tideover/lib/csv.ts:49, applied at tideover/lib/import.ts:69 and :101) — documented in-code as intentional ('sensible non-zero minimum ... never inflated beyond a floor') but it IS synthetic data feeding the gift-recommendation engine's `highValue = customer.ltvCents >= highTierCents` gate (tideover/lib/engines/gift.ts:31). Recommendation: rename/reframe the field in merchant-facing copy from 'lifetime value' to 'pledge value' for KS/BackerKit-sourced customers, and/or change import.ts to accumulate `ltvCents` across all of a customer's orders (sum of orderValueCents) rather than freezing at first import — small, scoped fix, no architecture change. ADR-0010 already states Shopify order-API pull and cross-merchant/live scraping are explicitly out of scope/cut (docs/adr/ADR-0010-csv-import.md lines 25-27), so CSV-only is the intended end state for this rail, not a temporary stub.
